texts: When an LAD lesion is hard to judge on angiography, especially with a short left main where the catheter slips into the LAD and damps the pressure, the next step is fractional flow reserve.
FFR compares the pressure beyond the narrowing with the pressure before it during maximal flow; a ratio of 0.80 or less means the lesion is significant.
It turns an uncertain picture into a number that decides whether the LAD needs a graft.
With a 90% right coronary lesion and a 70% circumflex already, knowing whether the LAD is significant shapes the whole plan.
In the picture, Chopper carries a small dial across the foggy narrowing and reads it against the dial before it.
Memory hook: when fog hides the slide, read two dials.
